prose: A Q&A with Timnit Gebru, who argues the 'existential risk' narrative is a harmful distraction. The piece retraces her arc: the Google departure over the stochastic-parrots paper, founding her institute for investigating tech harms, and her upcoming book Deep Unlearning: The Rise of AI and the Radicalization of a Tech Idealist. It frames the current fight as ideological rather than technical: doomers, including an Anthropic cofounder, now claim her stochastic-parrots critique is obsolete because AI can 'think', while her long-running critique of the effective-altruism community's cult-like dynamics has put her in strange alignment with right-wing critics of the same groups.
highlights: Gebru calls the 'existential risk' narrative a harmful distraction
Her book Deep Unlearning ships early next year
The stochastic-parrots paper cost her the Google job and founded her public profile
Doom-adjacent researchers, including an Anthropic cofounder, say her critique is obsolete because AI can 'think'
Her EA-community critique now overlaps with right-wing attacks on the same groups
Frames the AI debate as ideological and narrative-driven, not just technical
